html:
A war from 1780 to 1784 between Britain and the Dutch Republic, fought mostly at sea and in the colonies. It showed how far Dutch power had fallen.

The cause was the American Revolutionary War. Dutch merchants were selling arms to the American rebels, and the Dutch were about to join the League of Armed Neutrality to protect their shipping. Britain struck first and declared war.

The Dutch navy had been neglected and could do little. Britain seized hundreds of Dutch merchant ships and took Dutch posts in the Caribbean, in India and on Sumatra, and attacked Dutch Ceylon. The one big sea battle, at the Dogger Bank in 1781, was a draw.

At the peace of 1784 the Dutch gave up Negapatnam in India and let British ships trade freely in the East Indies. The Dutch East India Company (VOC) had lost ships and income and never recovered from its debts; it was taken over by the state in 1796. The defeat fed the Patriot movement against the stadtholder. It marks the end of Amsterdam at the centre.
sum: A war from 1780 to 1784 between Britain and the Dutch Republic, fought mostly at sea and in the colonies. It showed how far Dutch power had fallen.
